content.text: {"headline":"Recommend P0 (no action): overall service level is predicted at 81.7%, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"The spike is driven by the P1 UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998). 213 payments calls arrived at 10:30 against 111.9 forecast, and upi_payment_failed calls are running 2.56x normal. Staffing is at plan (42 of 43) and handle time is below forecast. With no changes, the forecast is 81.7% overall with 4.9% abandons. Payments is at 79.1% and general at 85.7%. P0 is the only option with no policy violations, and it already reaches the target overall.","trade_offs":["Payments is predicted at 79.1%, just under 80%, so payments callers carry the most risk if the outage drags on or volumes rise again.","P1 (no cost, 81.8%) barely improves on P0 and breaks policy. It delays a second break for 7 agents and drops general to 44-45% during the moves, below the 70% floor.","P2 (₹252, 83.2%, payments 80.3%, abandons 4.1%) is the cheapest way to lift payments above 80%. It still breaks BRK-04 (7 agents with more than one break delayed).","P3 (₹6,192) and P4 (₹7,020) reach about 91-92% with 1.8% abandons but cost far more and also breach BRK-04. P3 additionally pushes general to 64% during its move window."],"watch":"Watch the payments queue each interval and the status of the UPI incident. If payments service level slips below 80% or arrivals climb again, revisit P2 as the low-cost containment step, noting it needs a BRK-04 exception."}
